name: What jq Does
key_idea: jq reads JSON, runs a filter on it and prints JSON. A filter takes a value in and gives a value out. `.` is the whole input.

name: Reading JSON
key_idea: JSON has six kinds of value: string, number, boolean, null, array and object. Values nest, and you read them from the outside in.

name: Read a Value from an Object
key_idea: `.key` takes the value stored under a key. A missing key gives `null`, so an unexpected `null` often means a spelling mistake.

name: Go Deeper with a Path
key_idea: Join steps with dots to walk into nested objects: `.a.b.c`. Each step works on what the step before gave.

name: Pick an Item from a List
key_idea: `.[0]` takes the first item of an array, `.[-1]` the last, and `.[1:3]` a shorter array. An index is one more step in a path.

name: Chain Steps with a Pipe
key_idea: `a | b` runs `a`, then runs `b` on what `a` gave. After a pipe, `.` is the output of the step before. Named filters such as `length` work on their input.

name: Work on Every Item
key_idea: `.[]` takes an array apart: every item becomes its own output. What follows the pipe then runs once for each item.

name: Collect Results into a List
key_idea: Square brackets around a filter collect all its outputs into one array: `[.[] | .name]`.

name: Change Every Item with map
key_idea: `map(f)` runs `f` on every item of an array and gives a new array. It is short for `[.[] | f]`.

name: Ask Yes-or-No Questions
key_idea: `==`, `!=`, `<` and `>=` compare two values and give `true` or `false`. `and`, `or` and `not` join tests.

name: Keep Only Some Items
key_idea: `select(test)` passes a value on when the test is true and drops it otherwise. Use it on each item, after `.[]` or inside `map`.

name: Count Things
key_idea: To count, first make an array of what you want, then take its `length`.

name: Build a New Object
key_idea: `{name: .user, id: .id}` builds a new object from parts of the input. `{id}` is short for `{id: .id}`.

name: Ask for Several Things at Once
key_idea: `a, b` gives the outputs of `a`, then the outputs of `b`, from the same input.

name: Build Text from Values
key_idea: Inside a string, `\(filter)` is replaced by the filter's output: `"\(.name) is \(.age)"`.

name: Plain Text with -r
key_idea: jq prints strings as JSON, with quotes. The `-r` flag prints them as plain text, ready for other tools.

name: Rows for a Spreadsheet
key_idea: `@csv` and `@tsv` turn an array into one line of a table. Use them with `-r`.

name: Fill Gaps with a Default
key_idea: `a // b` gives `a`, unless `a` is `null` or `false`; then it gives `b`.

name: Skip What Does Not Fit
key_idea: `?` after a step hides its error: `.a?` gives nothing when the input is not an object.

name: Tell Value Kinds Apart
key_idea: `type` gives the kind of a value as a string, such as `"number"` or `"array"`.

name: Choose with if
key_idea: `if test then a else b end` gives `a` when the test is true and `b` otherwise.

name: Split and Join Text
key_idea: `split(",")` cuts a string into an array of parts. `join(",")` glues an array of strings into one string.

name: Match Text
key_idea: `test("regex")` is true when a string matches. `startswith`, `endswith` and `contains` cover the simple cases.

name: Replace Text
key_idea: `sub` replaces the first match and `gsub` every match. `ascii_downcase` and `ascii_upcase` change the case.

name: Convert Text and Numbers
key_idea: `tostring` turns a value into a string and `tonumber` turns a numeric string into a number. jq never converts by itself.

name: Sort a List
key_idea: `sort` orders an array. `sort_by(.field)` orders objects by a field. `reverse` turns the order around.

name: Totals, Smallest and Largest
key_idea: `add` adds up an array. `min` and `max` give the smallest and largest; `min_by` and `max_by` compare by a field.

name: Remove Repeats
key_idea: `unique` sorts an array and removes repeats. `unique_by(.field)` keeps one object for each value of the field.

name: Group Items
key_idea: `group_by(.field)` splits an array into groups, one array for each value of the field. Then `map` each group to a summary.

name: Objects as Lists of Pairs
key_idea: `to_entries` turns an object into an array of `{key, value}` pairs, and `from_entries` turns it back.

name: Change a Value in Place
key_idea: `path |= f` replaces the value at the path with `f` of the old value and keeps everything else.

name: Add and Merge with +
key_idea: `+` adds numbers, joins strings, joins arrays and merges objects.

name: Remove a Value
key_idea: `del(path)` gives the input without the value at that path.

name: Find a Value at Any Depth
key_idea: `..` gives the input and every value inside it, at any depth. Follow it with `select` or `.key?`.

name: One Line per Value with -c
key_idea: jq pretty-prints by default. The `-c` flag prints each output on one line, which line-based tools need.

name: Pass Values into a Filter
key_idea: `--arg name value` gives the filter a string variable `$name`. `--argjson` passes a JSON value.

name: Many Inputs in One File
key_idea: A file may hold many JSON values, one per line. jq runs the filter once per value. The `-s` flag reads them all into one array first.

name: Name a Value
key_idea: `value as $x | ...` gives a value a name, so you can keep something from the outer input while you work on an inner part.

name: Carry a Result Along
key_idea: `reduce .[] as $x (start; update)` walks the items and carries one result along.

name: Your Own Filters
key_idea: `def name: body;` gives a filter a name, so a long program reads in small steps.
